$comment: Code Puppy authority registry (#1662 L4; coordinator instruction 2026-11-09: 'every decision Code Puppy makes today must still be Code Puppy's after the OpenCode 2 switch').

One entry per decision. Held entries name the OpenCode 2 mechanism file and the tests that turn red when the mechanism is removed; blocked entries carry the reason and the options awaiting the orchestrator.

An entry is never deleted: retiring one needs `retired: { quote, date, by }` with the owner's words. Judge: packages/ext/src/policy/authority-registry.test.ts (coverage of the 49 pre-switch takeovers, files and test names exist, no blocked entry, no deletion).

anchor.note: origin/alpha before the switch; `scripts/north-star-guard.sh --print-takeover` there is the 49-path list every takeover must map to.

entries.decision: Every tool call passes Code Puppy's tool policy before it runs; a deny is a named refusal decided before any other hook or side effect (#725 B, #1129).

tests.name: B1 MCP deny ⇒ named refusal and the call never reaches the tool
deny is decided first: the extension's own execute.before never sees a denied call
reverse arm ①: without registerPolicy the same denied calls execute (group B would be red)
Code Mode child call to a denied tool is refused
post-seal hook on the extension's own Context never sees a denied call, which stays refused by name
post-seal known-bad arm: without registerPolicy the same late hooks rewrite the input and run the denied tool

entries.decision: A call whose tool identity cannot be established is refused (baseline S1: unknown identity defaults to deny).

tests.name: unknown tool identity is refused by default

entries.decision: Hooks running after Code Puppy's approval cannot rewrite the approved tool or input (baseline S1, ruling R8 option 2).

tests.name: reverse arm ②: a plugin after seal() that rewrites the input cannot run the call
reverse arm ② control: the same late plugin leaving input alone lets the call run
post-seal hook on the extension's own Context: a rewrite of the approved input cannot run the call

entries.decision: The model never sees a tool the policy denies, neither as a direct tool nor in the Code Mode catalog (#725 A, ruling F6).

mechanism.ladder: L0 (agent rules after configured ones + session.hook.context)

tests.name: A4 + F6: one MCP tool denied ⇒ gone from the Code Mode catalog too; its sibling stays
F6 reverse arm: without Code Puppy's catalog rules the denied MCP tool is back in Code Mode
first request before the tail rules exist: denied direct tools are pruned, Code Mode is withheld
A6 ask never changes the catalog

entries.decision: A document-axis ask waits for the user through OpenCode's permission engine with Code Puppy's identity envelope; nothing runs before approval; once/always keep their meaning; no other plugin's evaluate hook can turn Code Puppy's ask into allow.

mechanism.ladder: L0 (tail ask rule; gate.ts holdAsk from the early evaluate hook)

tests.name: document-axis ask ⇒ one identity request with the I7a envelope; reject keeps the count at 0
approved once ⇒ the call runs exactly once
ruleset-axis ask ⇒ askedBy ruleset, a per-call resource, nothing saved
post-seal evaluate hook on the extension's own Context cannot turn Code Puppy's ask into allow
post-seal evaluate hook may still make Code Puppy's ask stricter: deny refuses without a prompt
post-seal evaluate known-bad arm: the same late hook does turn an ask that is not Code Puppy's into allow

entries.note: An answer to the pending request itself is not held here: any plugin Context (including the extension's, which the project-plugin fan-out passes through) can call permission.reply on Code Puppy's request and the call runs (measured 2026-11-09); closing it belongs to the fan-out (L3), reported to the coordinator.

entries.decision: An always approval is bound to the service binding and the policy revision; any policy write asks again (#1128, #1574).

tests.name: an always approval discharges the next ask for the same binding and revision; a policy write re-asks

entries.decision: Deny is a ceiling: a ruleset deny on the exact identity folds into the cap, and no user enable or saved approval opens it (#1128 / #724 §4).

tests.name: ruleset-axis identity deny (agent rule on the canonical) hides the tool the same way
R8/R9/R10/R11 fail-closed 族:非法 identity / quarantine / managed unreadable / 冲突记录 ⇒ disabled

entries.decision: Organisation (managed / MDM) denies are an unbreakable cap — a project agent rule cannot out-rank them.

tests.name: M1 a managed deny is a cap even when the merged agent ruleset ends with a project allow (why the reader exists)
M4 a corrupt managed file, or a JSONC one this reader cannot parse, makes the whole layer unreadable ⇒ disabled

entries.decision: The user policy document: three states, exact tool > service > class, binding guard, whole-document quarantine on any bad record (#1128 / #724 §2–§5).

tests.name: R6 binding guard:service/tool enabled 只在 digest 逐字相等时生效,变了/缺了回 ask(§5)
T3 坏文档整份 quarantine:损坏 JSON / 未知版本 / 部分非法记录 / 分区不符 / selector 重复

entries.decision: Policy is partitioned per signed-in account and per folder (outside git) / per project (inside git) (#1575, #1644).

tests.name: AC2 subdirectories of one git project share its grant; different git projects stay isolated
VI1 the account partition follows CODEPUPPY_POLICY_ACCOUNT: account B never reads account A's enable

entries.decision: The composer tier's tool-policy-default decides whether class-default asks apply (I9, #1638).

tests.name: I9: tool-policy-default allow waives the class-default ask; ask keeps it

entries.decision: Settings reads and writes the tool policy through Code Puppy's API (v1 routes /api/permission/tool-policy/*; OpenCode 2 plugin RPC codepuppy.tool-policy, I5).

tests.name: inventory returns a document that decodes as ToolPolicyInventoryV1
I2 the badge tells the truth: a tool the inventory shows disabled is refused by the production executor
a quarantined document ⇒ setRecord fails with type quarantined
reverse arm: without registerPolicy the RPC is unavailable

entries.decision: Renamed builtins (bash→shell, task→subagent, apply_patch→patch): saved records under the old name keep applying and are reported; classification knows both names (K5 / S4).

tests.name: a saved deny under the v1 name refuses the renamed tool, and the record is reported
a deny under the new name refuses the call

entries.decision: Every approval request carries Code Puppy's rule-based risk classification, overriding what a tool reports (#1285 / REQ-158).

tests.name: a forged metadata.codepuppyRisk is overwritten: shell `rm -rf /` claims low, the pending request says high/destructive
the premise check is not empty: a synthetic engine that creates a request without evaluating fails it
every approval request carries Code Puppy's risk classification, overriding what the tool reported (#1285)

entries.decision: Each tool's identity (source, origin, name) is decided by Code Puppy from registration facts, never from aliases or titles.

mechanism.ladder: L0 (early registry + MCP config + bundled manifest)

tests.name: an MCP tool: config key as origin, remote tool name, de-secreted binding, remote location and transport
a tool in the early registry is a builtin with the constant application binding and local location
the MCP rule wins over the early registry (a server whose tools registered before the extension is still MCP)

entries.note: Derived from observable facts; collision/shadow detection is a separate, blocked entry (adr041-collision-rejection).

entries.decision: Only Code Puppy mints codepuppy-cloud / codepuppy-bundled authority, and only from the verified definition or the bundled manifest (ADR-041 §5, #1578).

tests.name: the exact verified cloud definition mints codepuppy-cloud with a sha256 evidence digest
a look-alike (same URL, other key; or same key, other URL) is not asserted
the exact bundled Office command next to the attested server.py mints codepuppy-bundled
listed own tools of a module whose digest matches get codepuppy-bundled; a project tool merged in does not

entries.decision: Each tool call carries Code Puppy's immutable display snapshot (identity, technicalId, authority, location) — OpenCode 2 state.metadata.codepuppyDisplay (I7b).

tests.name: running (progress) and completed (result metadata) carry the snapshot
a refused call's error carries the snapshot
the display snapshot is the schema's ToolDisplaySnapshotV1: identity + technicalId + authority + location

entries.decision: Where a tool runs (local, or the remote MCP host) is decided by Code Puppy from the de-secreted effective definition (#1576, #1617).

tests.name: a local MCP tool: local location, command transport, binding over command + cwd
document-axis ask ⇒ one identity request with the I7a envelope; reject keeps the count at 0

entries.decision: Authority and class values are codepuppy-* only, and the schema is their single definition (#1568 AC3).

tests.name: OpenCode 2's generated client types carry no copy of ToolAuthority (the schema is the only one)

entries.decision: A {workspace} token in an MCP command is replaced with the current folder when the server starts (#1011 / REQ-134).

tests.name: {workspace} in a local MCP command becomes the Location directory (#1011); without the policy it stays literal

tests.name: skips unusable tools and keeps the rest of the server's tools

#1047: error page uses the Code Puppy product identity

entries.decision: Code Puppy-owned files living under upstream paths are recognised by name or marker, and a copied marker does not exempt an upstream file (ADR-043).

entries.decision: The OpenCode 2 engine facts Code Puppy's receipt derivation relies on stay true: a pending request's payload cannot change under its id, one reply emits a replied event for every request it resolves, and a second reply is NotFound (ruling item 1 measurements).

tests.name: (i) a pending request's payload never changes under its id: a second admission with the same id is refused
(ii) one always reply emits a replied event for every request it resolves, and only those
(ii) a reject cascades to every pending request of the same session, each with its own replied event
(iii) a second reply to the same id is NotFound: the engine keeps no reply history

entries.decision: Code Puppy owns the approval reply contract: a sha256 fingerprint of the displayed request, a DecisionReceipt for every reply listing the requests it resolved, idempotent replay, and a 409 on a stale reply (#433 / REQ-090 AC3/AC8).

blocked.reason: Held by derivation in the L6 adapter (measurements passed, no kernel re-take; no production reader needs persisted history after a restart): spec in docs/architecture/2026-11-09-1662-permission-reply-measurements.md. Waiting on L6 to implement it.
options: Register L6's adapter file and its tests (re-read 409, replied-event resolved set, decisionID cache, each with a known-bad arm) when #1668 lands.

entries.decision: An unanswered approval request fails by name after a deadline (300 s default, CODEPUPPY_PERMISSION_ASK_TIMEOUT_MS override, invalid values fall back to the default) and never auto-allows; only that request ends (#668).

mechanism.ladder: L3 (re-taken: the wait on the reply is inside the kernel; a plugin watchdog's reject cascades)

tests.name: an unanswered request fails by name at the deadline, its card is retracted, and nothing is allowed
only that request ends: another pending request of the same session is still waiting (no cascade)
the default is 300 s and every invalid override falls back to it, never to no deadline

entries.decision: A model route whose deployment declared no credential refuses before the socket opens instead of sending an unauthenticated request (#652, owner ruling 2026-07-28 per the v1 source comment).

mechanism.ladder: L3 (re-taken: a plugin cannot change route defaults; Auth.unset in route/auth.ts, chat and decision defaults, no template-level Auth.none on the two OpenAI protocols)

tests.name: a route that never declared auth refuses before the socket opens
the OpenAI Responses template deployed without auth refuses before the socket opens too
a decision route that never declared auth refuses before the socket opens
an explicitly declared Auth.none still sends — the gate is a declaration, not a ban
a declared credential that resolves to nothing also refuses before the socket opens
every provider entry built with no credential sends nothing without one

entries.note: Audit 2026-11-09: all 94 provider entries with a model factory already refused without a credential before the re-take; the other four protocol templates (anthropic-messages, gemini, google-interactions, mistral-chat) keep a template-level Auth.none that no production construction path reaches without its own credential (held by the pin). Not covered: packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts declares Auth.none itself for a configured provider with no key and no connection (keyless local providers) — an explicit engine-side declaration, reported to the coordinator.
